title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
body: Discovered in 1947 in caves near Qumran, the Dead Sea Scrolls include the oldest known copies of Old Testament books, some over 2,000 years old — confirming the remarkable accuracy of the text handed down through generations.

title: The Printing Press and the Bible
body: The first major book printed on Gutenberg's printing press around 1455 was the Bible, making Scripture far more accessible than the hand-copied manuscripts that came before it.

title: Written Across Three Continents
body: The Bible was written over roughly 1,500 years by more than 40 authors across Asia, Africa, and Europe — from shepherds and kings to physicians and fishermen.

title: The Most Translated Book
body: The Bible has been translated, in whole or in part, into more than 3,500 languages — more than any other book in human history.

title: Jerusalem's Long Memory
body: Jerusalem has been destroyed and rebuilt multiple times over roughly 3,000 years of recorded history, yet it remains central to the story of Scripture from Genesis to Revelation.

title: The Synagogue at Capernaum
body: Ruins of a synagogue still stand in Capernaum, believed to sit atop the very synagogue where Jesus taught and healed, as recorded in the Gospels.

title: Early Church Catacombs
body: Beneath Rome, early Christians met and buried their dead in catacombs, leaving behind some of the earliest Christian art — simple symbols of fish, anchors, and shepherds.
